The company relies on the human-appeal exception instead of offering a full ADMT opt-out. The CPPA's regulations set a specific, three-part standard for the reviewer that exception depends on (11 CCR § 7221(b)(2)(A)). In its Final Statement of Reasons, the Agency described the standard directly: the reviewer "must know how to interpret and use the output of the ADMT that made the significant decision being appealed," must review that output together with any other information relevant to the decision, and must have actual authority to change the decision. A reviewer who can only rubber-stamp or forward the ADMT's output — without the knowledge or the authority to actually change it — does not satisfy this exception, even if an appeal process nominally exists. Section 4 addresses whether this company's appeal reviewer meets all three parts of this standard. (California Privacy Protection Agency, Final Statement of Reasons, CCPA Updates, Cyber, Risk, ADMT, and Insurance Regulations, 11 CCR § 7221(b)(2)(A), p. 49.)
